widgets_values: Describe the key features of the reference image (color, shape, size, texture, objects, background), then explain how the user's instruction should combine with or alter it, and generate a new image meeting the instruction while staying consistent with the reference where appropriate:

Photorealistic portrait.
Natural skin texture.
Realistic eyes.
Realistic hair.
Professional DSLR photograph.

nodes.title: Text String (System Prompt)
widgets_values:
You are an expert prompt engineer for text-to-image models. Your task is to expand the user's prompt into a highly effective image-generation prompt.

Think step by step about the request before writing the answer:
- What is the subject and mood?
- What visual styles, mediums, and lighting options would fit? Consider two or three alternatives and pick the one that best serves the caption.
- What composition, framing, and grounded details will help the text-to-image model?

Then output a single expanded prompt paragraph.

Follow these rules strictly:
1. **Faithfulness First:** Preserve all original subjects, actions, colors, and spatial relationships. Do not add new objects, props, characters, or animals unless the user clearly implies them.
2. **Practical T2I Structure:** Write a prompt that a text-to-image model can parse cleanly. Group subjects with their own attributes and actions. Use grounded phrasing for poses, interactions, and spatial layout.
3. **Style Planning Stays Internal:** Use your internal reasoning to choose style, medium, framing, and lighting. Do not emit planning tags or wrappers in the visible answer body.
4. **Avoid Over-Specification:** Do not invent highly specific clothing, colors, materials, or scene details unless the input supports them.
5. **Structure:** Write one cohesive paragraph after the thinking block. No bullets, JSON, or markdown.
6. **Respect Existing Detail:** If the user's prompt is already detailed, lightly polish and finalize rather than heavily expanding — preserve their phrasing and direction.
7. **Convert image into Realistic descriptions:** Change things like "digital illustration" and "semi-realistic" into realistic styled descriptors like "realistic" and "realistic photograph"
8. Reference the included image in improving this prompt.

User's Input:

nodes.title: Note about Prompt Generation
widgets_values:
Because manually prompting the contents of the image can be so difficult, I've provided two optional prompt generation approaches you can take here. - The Automatic Image Prompting section uses the already loaded Qwen CLIP to analyze the image internally, never producing a text prompt. This is normally intended as a pseudo image-to-image output (as Florence 2 lacks true I2I), but also serves our purposes well as we're able to use it to generate realistic style conversions. - However, a downside here is that since it never produces a text prompt, we're not able to see or tweak what it's doing. Even so, it does a reasonable job, and is the best option for quick anime-to-real style conversion.
- The Prompt Generation section also uses the already loaded Qwen CLIP to analyze the image to produce a prompt. - For NSFW prompts, you will need the [Abliterated text encoder](https://huggingface.co/ahmed22xa/Huihui-Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-abliterated-comfy/tree/main), as the normal text encoder is censored. - This is intended to be ran individually and manually, by clicking on the "preview as text" node and pressing run, and then copy-pasting that into the positive prompt and cleaning it up before running the rest of the workflow.

nodes.title: About Configuring This Prompt
widgets_values:
Altering the System Prompt doesn't have any meaningful effect, no matter how differently you try to word it.

The only way to steer the output here is the user prompt section, describing what you want to change about the image.

In our case, that's making it more realistic.

nodes.title: Note about these nodes
widgets_values: If you want to use these, you may need to download the nodes from the [github page](https://github.com/ethanfel/ComfyUI-Krea2TextEncoder)

nodes.title: Note about Samplers
widgets_values:
I've provided two k-sampler setups you can use in this workflow. A basic one. And a 2-pass advanced one to get the best quality.

By default I've disabled the 2-pass k-sampler. To enable it, select the nodes and Ctrl+B

nodes.title: Note about Models
widgets_values:
This workflow is by-default set up using the full Krea 2 Raw model with the Turbo LoRA at 0.6 strength, which provides good quality at reasonable (but a bit slow) speeds.

However, you can use any of the Krea 2 models with this workflow. Just swap out the models and adjust the samplers to your liking.

nodes.title: Note about Negative Prompting
widgets_values:
Negative prompts become ineffective at 1 CFG, which is what Turbo models/loras are built around.

However, if using the Raw Krea 2 model with the Turbo LoRA at 0.6 strength, higher CFG can still be used.

Increasing CFG to 2 seems to work well if you want negative prompting. But generations will take twice as long.

nodes.title: Note about Noise Amount
widgets_values:
This affects the balance between the source image and generated image. The higher the value, the more the samplers override the input image.

In my experience:
- 0.4 works well for detail refinement on semi-realistic images.
- 0.5 has an uncanny blend between stylized and realistic.
- 0.55 - 0.6 achieves good realism while retaining the composition of the source image.
- 0.65 begins to drift towards the composition of the generated image.
- 0.7 - 0.75 varies in quality depending on the generation; how good it looks largely depends on how good the full sampler image itself looks.
- 0.8+ typically drifts too far from the source image.
___________

What I like to do is start on 0.6, and then experiment with 0.75 for more realism, and 0.4 for more style.
